sentences.text: This meeting is being recorded.
Hi, Justin.
Hey, Andy, how's it going?
Yeah, good, thank you.
How are you doing?
One sec.
Can you hear me?
Can.
Yep.
Okay.
Sorry about that.
I got, got stuck on a call and I totally lost, lost track of time there, so.
My bad.
Yeah.
Yeah.
So I think Billy got in touch with you.
So I guess quickly I'll just introduce the firm.
So we're PNBC Holdings.
We're a publicly listed investment holding company listed on the NASDAQ Diversified.
So looking to add actively added acquisitions to our portfolio.
And right now we're looking for a marketing agency between like 300 to $500,000 asking price.
Probably somewhere between like, I would say $50,000 plus in EBITDA.
Okay.
Yeah.
Is there any particular type of marketing agency you're looking for, kind of work are they doing?
Not specifically.
Maybe.
Maybe marketing agencies.
I would, I would say that are working with like, with businesses like B.
A B.
Sorry, in particular.
What, what type of businesses there Are you just basically not really worried about what it currently does, just that it is in the marketing.
Yeah, not too much.
Just I.
Basically we want people that are, you know, really good at what they do.
Doesn't really matter if you're working in, I don't know, like the chicken farming industry.
You'll probably be good at another industry too if you're, if you're good at marketing in general.
But we're mainly looking at like industrial type businesses.

So people that are, you know, could I guess create a strategy for, you know, growing your customer base from like a, you know, recurring customer contract type of, type of approach or acquiring new customers.
Okay, so acquiring new customers would be like more like a lead gen or marketing.
Doing digital marketing.
Maybe.
Is it paid advertising that you would be looking for or.
All the above.
Okay, cool.
All right.
And it's a particularly small agency that you're, you're looking for.
Yeah, you know, they're probably hard to find, but yeah, probably we would want to max out at like $500,000.
Okay.
Yeah, they did come up.
You're.
I mean, it's at the low end of the market, but there, there are definitely agencies out there.
So I don't think we've got anything that's exactly that right now, but I will have a little bit of a look around.
But we are, we are capital A group and we have a marketing agency marketplace called Agencies Co.
I've just put the, the link in there.
I don't know whether you're aware of it, but basically if you sign up to our mailing list there.
Every time we have a new agency listed, then you'll get contacted with the teaser.
So it's probably worth signing up to there.
In the first instance, we've probably put about five or six agencies live over the last week or two.
So there's definitely a lot of activity.
I just don't think we've got anything as small as you're looking for.
But I will keep my eyes open because there's not a huge amount of buyers for tiny agencies.
And if that's what you're looking for, then potentially we could refer all of those to you.
I mean the only thing in that price range really that we've just onboarded is a PR company that's based in Georgia.
I don't know whether that would be a fit, but their valuation is 750 000.
But they would do some paid marketing as well as PR.
What do you, what do these things trade at from like a, even a multiple standpoint?
A small agency would be 4, 4 to 6 multiple.
Definitely at the lower end of that, the prices that you, you're, you're talking about.
But agencies can go.
We've sold an agency for 14 and a half times multiple.
So it really depends what sector they're in and what type of work they're doing.
There's a lot of variation.
Yeah.
What, what about the PR one, What are they, what's their multiple based on the asking?
So their multiple is 4.1.
Okay, that's pretty good.
I'll send you the link as well here.
So you'd have to look for it when you get on the site.
Interesting.
And are most of these like, what's the reason for sale would you say?
Are people just looking to retire?
All different types of reasons.
In this instance it is much closer to a retirement sale.
The link that I've just sent you to the PR company, but it is all sorts of different reasons.

Sometimes owners, because they tend to be quite creative people, they just end up wanting to work in a larger organization so they don't have to do all of the business stuff that can be a common reason.

Sometimes they're just really ambitious and they kind of hit a ceiling of where they can grow on their own and they just want to get into a company that has access to more resources so they can grow more quickly.
But yeah, I mean it's quite an established business.

For, for probably 50, 60 years, marketing agencies have existed in this kind of bubble where people leave large agencies, create their own ones and Then they get bought out again by the, the holding companies.
So it's fairly common outcome for most agency owners.
Interesting.
Yeah, I can understand how they would want to, they're creative, right.
They want to, don't want to be doing like bookkeeping and stuff.
That's kind of where we can add value.
Like we could take over the accounting and legal and then they just focus on, you know, what they're good at.
So.
And then also like we want to, so we have existing portfolio companies and we want to use them for our marketing as well.
So automatically like they would grow their customer list.
Okay, well this PR company could be a good option for you.
The founder is extremely experienced.
She actually sold a large agency in the UK before she relocated to the US So it's a very established agency in that area.
But they could quite easily with their team pick up and handle more work.
Like you say, it doesn't really matter where it comes from.
They would be able to, to handle it.
Okay, interesting.

Are these usually like all cash up front deals, these type, these acquisitions for these marketing companies or would they be open to like, like 90 or 80 cash up front and then the rest like milestone payments or something like that?
Yeah, we'd, we'd certainly take a look at a deal with a 80 or 90% cash up front offer.
Certainly especially for the smaller ones.
Like you're talking.
Yeah, interesting.
Okay, awesome.
Yeah, that sounds good.
Well, we'll take a deeper look at this one and get back to you.
I think it's pretty interesting especially if they're open to structuring the deal.
So it's not 100% upfront.
Yeah, yeah, let me, let me know what you think.
I mean they would be, they would be happy to do a deal, I think just to get it over the line.
Like I said, she's extremely experienced in the solar business before, so she'd be used to some kind of structure in that.
And is she wanting to stay on or what does she want to sell?
So it is a retirement sale of sorts.
However, she's, she's not keen to leave.
I mean she's by no means does.
She's considering herself an old lady yet.
I think she's in her mid to late 50s, but yeah, she's got another 10 years in her potentially.
So I think if the right buyer came along and she had an opportunity to work in a larger organization for a while, I think she would definitely consider staying.
In fact, we had a buyer that is interested offer something similar.
They actually want to do exactly what you want to do.
They want to put their own contracts through her, and she.
She said she would be interested, so I think it would just boils down to who the buyer is.
Okay.
Have they.
Has that other buyer.
Have they submitted an loi?
Yeah.
You've got a great opportunity at the moment because he is actually also the guy that wants to or is interested in buying.
He's having a retirement sale over the next two or three years himself, and he has a.
What would you call her?
A managing director already in place, and she is kind of overwhelmed with a lot of the work that she has on at the moment.
They've just had a senior person quit, so he is giving her two or three weeks to get over this workload before they make a decision.
So we're kind of in.
We're in a gap right now where you could come in and just steal it, so.
Okay.
Okay.
Yeah, that's really interesting.
We'll.
We'll take a look.
Okay, awesome.
Thanks a lot, Andy.
All right.
Thanks for hopping on, Justin.
I'll follow up in a couple of days and see where you're at.
Sweet.
Okay, sounds good.
Thanks.
All right, brilliant.
Enjoy the rest of your day.
Just.

summary.overview: In a recent Business Development and Acquisition meeting, Justin Roadhouse from PNBC Holdings and Andy Day from Capital A Group discussed PNBC's interest in acquiring a marketing agency valued between $300,000 and $500,000, emphasizing a preference for B2B marketing agencies that demonstrate a capacity for generating recurring customer contracts with a minimum EBITDA of $50,000. The meeting highlighted the competitive landscape for agency acquisitions, with multiples ranging from 4 to 14.5 times earnings depending on the sector, and discussed a specific PR company opportunity based in Georgia that is currently available due to the founder's move towards semi-retirement. Justin outlined PNBC's value proposition, which includes managing accounting and legal aspects to allow creative teams to excel, and sought clarification on flexible deal structures. Action items from the discussion included Justin's review of the PR company opportunity and signing up for Agency Co's mailing list, while Andy committed to following up on the discussed opportunities.
summary.short_summary: In a recent meeting, Justin Roadhouse from PNBC Holdings and Andy Day from Capital A Group explored PNBC's interest in acquiring a marketing agency valued between $300,000 and $500,000. They highlighted a preference for B2B marketing agencies that can generate recurring customer contracts and have a minimum EBITDA of $50,000. The discussion covered the competitive landscape of agency acquisitions, where multiples can range from 4 to 14.5 times earnings based on the sector. A specific PR company opportunity in Georgia was also mentioned, available due to the founder's semi-retirement. Justin presented PNBC's value proposition, which involves managing the accounting and legal aspects, allowing creative teams to focus on their work. Action items included Justin reviewing the PR company opportunity and Andy committing to follow up on discussed opportunities.
